items.title: Section: The Single Moment Before Breakthrough — "Supreme Mundane Dharma," and How Not to Mistake Dullness for It

items.zh: 彼於爾時，其心似滅，而非實滅；似無所緣，而非無緣。又於爾時，其心寂靜，雖似遠離，而非遠離。又於爾時，非美睡眠之所覆蓋，唯有分明無高、無下奢摩他行。
items.en: At that time, the mind seems extinguished, yet is not actually extinguished; it seems to have no object, yet is not actually objectless. At that time, the mind is still, and though it seems detached, it is not actually detached. And at that time, the mind is not covered over by deep, dreamless sleep — there is only a lucid calm-abiding, neither elevated nor depressed.

items.zh: 復有一類，闇昧愚癡，於美睡眠之所覆蓋，其心似滅非實滅中，起增上慢，謂為現觀。此不如是。
items.en: There is, however, another kind of person who, dull and confused, covered over by a deep, dreamless sleep, gives rise, within that same seeming-but-not-actual extinction, to an inflated conceit, believing it to be genuine direct realisation. This is not what is meant here.

items.zh: 既得如是趣現觀心，不久當入正性離生。即於如是寂靜心位，最後一念無分別心，從此無間，於前所觀諸聖諦理，起內作意。此即名為世第一法。從此已後，出世心生，非世間心。此是世間諸行最後界畔邊際，是故名為世第一法。

items.title: Section: MAJOR — Genuine Breakthrough at Last, Delivering Three Different Fruits

items.zh: 從此無間，於前所觀諸聖諦理，起內作意；作意無間，隨前次第所觀諸諦，若是現見、若非現見諸聖諦中，如其次第，有無分別決定智、現見智生。由此生故，三界所繫見道所斷附屬所依諸煩惱品一切麁重，皆悉永斷。
items.en: Immediately following this, without any gap, one gives rise to an inward engagement with respect to the principle of the noble truths already observed; and this engagement, without any gap, following the same sequence already observed … gives rise, in due order, to a non-discriminating, decisive wisdom — a wisdom of direct seeing. Because this arises, all the coarseness of the classes of affliction bound to the three realms, severed on the path of seeing, and attached to their basis, is permanently and entirely cut off.

items.zh: 此永斷故，若先已離欲界貪者，彼於今時既入如是諦現觀已，得不還果。彼與前說離欲者相，當知無異。然於此中少有差別。謂當受化生，即於彼處當般涅槃，不復還來生此世間。若先倍離欲界貪者，彼於今時既入如是諦現觀已，得一來果。若先未離欲界貪者，彼於今時既入如是諦現觀已，麁重永息，得預流果。
items.en: Because of this permanent severance: if one had already become free of desire-realm craving beforehand, then, having now entered this direct realisation of the truths, one attains the fruit of non-return … if one had already become more than halfway free of desire-realm craving, one attains the fruit of once-return … and if one had not yet become free of desire-realm craving at all, then, having now entered this direct realisation of the truths, the coarse afflictions are permanently stilled, and one attains the fruit of stream-entry.

items.title: What "Direct Realisation" Actually Means — Knower and Known, Finally of One Kind

items.zh: 由能知智與所知境和合無乖，現前觀察，故名現觀。如剎帝利與剎帝利和合無乖，現前觀察，名為現觀。婆羅門等，當知亦爾。
items.en: Because the knowing wisdom and the known object come together without any discord, directly observing one another, this is called direct realisation — just as a member of the ruling caste, together with another of the same ruling caste, comes together without any discord, directly recognising one another, is called direct realisation; the same should be understood for a member of the priestly caste and the like.

items.title: Same Outward Calm, Different Inward Fate — and a Monk Who Mistook a Dead End for Liberation

items.en: That person's marks, one should know, are no different from the marks of one free of desire already described. Yet there is here a slight distinction: such a person will take spontaneous rebirth, and precisely there attain final nirvāṇa, never again returning to be reborn in this world.

items.title: Section: The Stream-Enterer's Marks — Four Knowledges, and a Lazy Brahmin Learns No One Can practise for Him

items.zh: 謂證如是諦現觀故，獲得四智。謂於一切若行、若住諸作意中，善推求故，得唯法智、得非斷智、得非常智、得緣生行如幻事智。若行境界，由失念故，雖起猛利諸煩惱纏，暫作意時，速疾除遣；又能畢竟不墮惡趣；終不故思違越所學，乃至傍生亦不害命；終不退轉，棄捨所學；不復能造五無間業；定知苦樂非自所作、非他所作、非自他作、非非自他無因而生；終不求請外道為師，亦不於彼起福田想；於他沙門、婆羅門等，終不觀瞻口及顏面；唯自見法、得法、知法、證法源底，越度疑惑，不由他緣；於大師教，非他所引；
items.en: Because of realising direct realisation of the truths, one attains four kinds of knowledge — knowledge of mere phenomena, knowledge of non-annihilation, knowledge of non-permanence, and knowledge that conditioned processes are like an illusion … one alone sees the phenomenon, attains the phenomenon, knows the phenomenon, and fathoms the phenomenon to its very source, crossing beyond doubt, not by reliance on another; with respect to the Teacher's own instruction, one is not led by anyone else.

items.zh: 於諸法中得無所畏；終不妄計世瑞吉祥以為清淨；終不更受第八有生；具足成就四種證淨。如是行者，乃至世第一法已前，名勝解作意。於諸聖諦現觀已後，乃至永斷見道所斷一切煩惱，名遠離作意。復從
此後，為欲進斷修所斷惑，如所得道更數修習，永斷欲界上品、中品諸煩惱已，得一來果。如預流果所有諸相，今於
items.en: Homage to you, most valiant one in this human realm, a true and holy seeker, whose pure eye sees all things — may you remove my doubt! … I have, in truth, no power to free you from your doubt; only if you yourself see the excellent teaching will you cross beyond the flood.

blocks.text: The moment of breakthrough. This is the centre of the whole Śrāvaka Stage. A short passage (0475c20) is untranslated.

"At that time the mind seems extinguished, yet is not; seems to have no object, yet is not objectless; is still, and seems detached, yet is not." "The mind is not covered by pleasant drowsiness; there is only a lucid calm." But beware: "another kind of person, dull and confused, covered by deep sleep, gives rise within that seeming extinction to an inflated conceit, believing it to be direct realisation. This is not it."

"Immediately following this, without any gap", an inward engagement with the truths arises, and "every coarse affliction of the three realms abandoned on the path of seeing" is permanently cut. Then: one already free of desire-realm craving becomes a **non-returner**; one more than halfway free, a **once-returner**; one not yet free, a **stream-enterer**.
"The knowing wisdom and the known object come together without discord, directly observing one another: like a member of the ruling caste meeting another of the same caste."

The stream-enterer gains four knowledges: that there are only phenomena; that they are not annihilated; that they are not permanent; that conditioned things are like an illusion. "One alone sees the phenomenon, attains it, knows it." A verse closes the passage: someone begs the Buddha to remove his doubt, and the Buddha replies: "I have no power to free you from your doubt; only if you yourself see the excellent teaching will you cross over."

quiz.q: At the supreme mundane dharma, "not covered by pleasant drowsiness — only lucidity." How does Venerable Miào Jìng contrast it with ordinary sleep?
options: no discrimination at all, yet lucid
quiz.why: "And at that time, the mind is not covered over by pleasant drowsiness — there is only a lucid calm-abiding, neither elevated nor depressed." Venerable Miào Jìng: there's no discrimination at all, yet there is lucidity — so it differs from our ordinary sleep.

quiz.q: "Dull and confused, covered by pleasant drowsiness … believing it to be direct realisation." What example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: a fellow practitioner dozed while sitting, then said he'd practised very well
quiz.why: "There is, however, another kind of person who, dull and confused, covered over by a pleasant drowsiness, gives rise … to an inflated conceit, believing it to be genuine direct realisation." Master Cháng Bǎi: a fellow practitioner once dozed off while sitting, and afterwards said he'd practised very well.

quiz.q: "If one had already become free of desire-realm craving," entering direct realisation, "one attains non-return." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: not stream-entry, not once-return — straight to the third fruit
quiz.why: "Because of this permanent severance: if one had already become free of desire-realm craving beforehand, then, having now entered this direct realisation of the truths, one attains the fruit of non-return." Venerable Miào Jìng: he doesn't get the first fruit or the second — he gets the third all at once.

quiz.q: "If one had already 倍離 desire-realm craving … once-return" — rendered "more than halfway free." How do the masters read 倍離?
options: Miào Jìng: 倍 means "a portion"; Cháng Bǎi: six to eight of the desire realm's nine grades severed
quiz.why: "If one had already become more than halfway free of desire-realm craving, one attains the fruit of once-return." Venerable Miào Jìng: how is 倍 read here? As "a portion." Master Cháng Bǎi: one who has severed six to eight grades of the desire realm's afflictions of cultivation attains once-return. The English follows the latter reading.

quiz.q: Direct realisation is likened to "one of the ruling caste meeting another without discord." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain it?
options: I see you as kṣatriya, you see me as kṣatriya — observer and observed both non-self
quiz.why: "Just as a member of the ruling caste, together with another of the same ruling caste, comes together without any discord, directly recognising one another, is called direct realisation." Venerable Miào Jìng: I see you're a kṣatriya, you see I'm a kṣatriya — observer and observed are both the realm of non-self.

quiz.q: The non-returner "takes spontaneous rebirth … never returning to this world." What does Venerable Miào Jìng add?
options: with compassion, may return by vow to guide beings
quiz.why: "Such a person will take spontaneous rebirth, and precisely there attain final nirvāṇa, never again returning to be reborn in this world." Venerable Miào Jìng: if he has compassion and comes to the desire realm to guide beings, he can come — returning by vow.

quiz.q: One of the four knowledges: "conditioned processes are like an illusion." What image does Venerable Miào Jìng use?
options: a magician producing a rabbit from a handkerchief
quiz.why: "Knowledge of mere phenomena, knowledge of non-annihilation, knowledge of non-permanence, and knowledge that conditioned processes are like an illusion." Venerable Miào Jìng: he turns a small handkerchief into a rabbit.
